terminology.normative: A normative requirement uses MUST or MUST NOT and is eligible for conformance.
terminology.informative: An informative note explains scope or a gap and is not an acceptance claim.
terminology.verified: A verified claim has at least one executable gate and exact Threadleaf version.
terminology.notVerified: A not-verified claim is visible context and cannot be presented as passing.

claims.title: Same-vault behavior corpus
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: The checked-in corpus cases marked supported run through public kernel, application, and CLI surfaces.
limitations: An unsupported case remains unsupported and is not counted as a pass.

claims.title: Excalidraw format and round-trip corpus
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Native scenes, Markdown scene fences, opaque compressed payloads, attachments, and revision conflicts have explicit byte or semantic contracts.
limitations: The official Obsidian round-trip is an observed external oracle, not an executable Threadleaf gate, and is not counted as an executable pass.
The packaged plugin workflow is an exact release observation, not universal Excalidraw parity.

claims.title: Exact-version plugin evidence registry
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Only exact plugin and Threadleaf versions in the generated registry carry a measured level.
limitations: A package without an exact production-path fixture remains discovered at level 0.

claims.title: Theme and snippet catalog
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Contained theme and snippet discovery, bounded loading, CSS rejection, and watcher behavior.
limitations: Package lifecycle is offline and local-file-only; no network theme store or remote package source is claimed.

claims.title: Native command-line contract
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: The current versioned native CLI command IDs, syntax aliases, exit codes, and output contracts are executable without Electron or network access.
limitations: Familiar external CLI spellings are separate compatibility targets and may remain unsupported.

claims.title: Reviewed migration apply, recovery, and rollback
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Migration preview is bounded and read-only; reviewed selections apply only private Threadleaf state through a journal with interruption recovery and rollback conflict checks.
limitations: Apply and rollback never write .obsidian or vault Markdown bytes, and plugin code is not executed inside the transaction.

claims.title: Live Preview and source mapping
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Live, Source, and Read modes share canonical Markdown bytes, bounded UTF-16 source mappings, reveal rules, and explicit source fallbacks.
limitations: Duplicate or malformed footnotes, malformed or ambiguous tables, unknown or malformed math, HTML, diagrams, and inline Live Preview processors remain source-visible.

claims.title: JSON Canvas byte and editing boundary
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Canvas documents are parsed, rendered, edited, and saved through the recoverable vault boundary while preserving unrelated JSON structure and file bytes on no-op round trips.
limitations: Canvas editing is not a claim about arbitrary proprietary canvas extensions or unsupported node types.

claims.title: Workspace panes, docks, pop-outs, and settings
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Per-vault workspace panes, pinned tabs, docks, plugin pop-outs, application settings, and key bindings persist outside the vault with revision and recovery checks.
limitations: Private application state is not a portable vault format and is not written into .obsidian.

claims.title: Markdown processor compatibility
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Trusted desktop plugins can register bounded fenced-code and post-processing callbacks with deterministic ordering, context, failure, and child lifecycle behavior.
limitations: Inline Live Preview processors, arbitrary section partitioning, and plugin-owned network or filesystem adapters are unsupported.

claims.title: Exact plugin package inspection
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Exact package bytes and manifests are checked before activation, including static authority evidence, bounded trusted activation, registration inventory, cleanup, timeout, and disposable-root diffs.
limitations: Inspection and cleanup are not an OS sandbox; synchronous code, unobserved paths, and host authority outside the disposable root remain outside coverage.

claims.title: Native extension capability foundation
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Versioned manifests, exact bundle and authority digests, per-vault grants, typed capability ports, revocation, safe mode, deadlines, teardown, and cross-vault checks form the native foundation.
limitations: The first host is in-process and reports sandboxed: false; production bundle evaluation and OS process isolation are not wired into this foundation.
Desktop navigation, subprocess, secrets, and dynamic-code ports are trusted desktop escapes, not portable sandboxed capabilities.

claims.title: Public specification build
claims.label: normative
claims.scope: Generated tables, schemas, local links, anchors, fixture hashes, exact versions, and offline assets are checked together.
limitations: Publishing the generated site remains a maintainer-authorized operation.

gaps.title: Native extension production bundle wiring
gaps.label: informative
gaps.reason: The native capability host is exercised through a typed fixture entrypoint; production bundle evaluation and OS process isolation are not wired into this foundation.

gaps.title: Trusted community plugin sandbox
gaps.label: informative
gaps.reason: Community plugin inspection and grants make trust explicit but do not sandbox Node-capable plugin code or prove absence of omitted authority.

gaps.title: Universal community plugin parity
gaps.label: informative
gaps.reason: Compatibility is measured per exact release and named workflow; discovery, static inspection, or one plugin pass is not universal parity.
